name: Amantaka
positioning: Aman resort in a converted provincial hospital, beneath Mount Phousi in the UNESCO World Heritage town of Luang Prabang
best_for: Travelers who want a calm base in Luang Prabang's historic town
Guests interested in Lao Buddhist culture and arts

facts.text: Amantaka is at 55/3 Kingkitsarath Road, Ban Thongchaleun, Luang Prabang, Laos.
The drive from Luang Prabang International Airport to Amantaka is 10 minutes.
Amantaka sits beneath Mount Phousi, a stroll from the riverbank and the town's main street.
Amantaka is in Luang Prabang, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, at the foot of Mount Phousi amid golden spired wats and quaint lanes.
The resort takes its name from Tipitaka, meaning 'the teaching of Buddha'.
The resort has a swimming pool and a spa.
The property is a conversion of Luang Prabang's old provincial hospital.
The colonial-style lobby, under a low red-tiled roof, is the former X-ray room.
The bigger suites have private pools.
Decor uses simple Southeast Asian wood furnishings, an embroidered silk throw and black-and-white photographs of Buddhist monks in meditation.

highlights.text: The town's experts in Theravada Buddhism, traditional arts and ethnology are on call for guests.
Guests get access to a photographic archive of monastic life dating back to the 1880s.
A member of the former royal family is on hand to discuss Lao fine arts.
Guided walks lead away from the main sights to explore abandoned temples.

considerations.text: The hotel has a slight sanitarium feel, with long corridors and tiny ward-like chambers.
The interior is pared down to the point of austere, in contrast to the town's gilded temples.
WhataHotel notes limited nightlife and entertainment options in the historic Luang Prabang setting.
